questions.title: Section A: Multiple Choice, Matching, Terminology and True/False

subQuestions.questionText: A thick-walled stomach which helps to grind food with small stones is found in …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C - fowls (2 marks)
The gizzard (ventriculus) of a fowl is a thick, muscular stomach that grinds food, aided by grit / small stones the bird swallows.

subQuestions.questionText: The stomach compartments in ruminant animals that are responsible for microbial digestion:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B - Rumen and reticulum (2 marks)
Microbial (fermentative) digestion of roughage takes place in the rumen and reticulum, which together contain the fermentation micro-organisms. The omasum absorbs water and the abomasum is the true (enzymatic) stomach.

subQuestions.questionText: The Pearson square in the question paper shows maize meal (8% CP) at the top-left corner, fish meal (32% CP) at the bottom-left corner and a desired value of 12% in the centre. The following is the ratio to which the two feeds should be mixed:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B - 20 parts of maize meal to 4 parts of fish meal (2 marks)
Maize meal parts = 32 − 12 = 20; fish meal parts = 12 − 8 = 4. So the mix is 20 parts maize meal to 4 parts fish meal.

options.A: 8 parts of maize meal to 32 parts of fish meal
options.B: 20 parts of maize meal to 4 parts of fish meal
options.C: 4 parts of maize meal to 20 parts of fish meal
options.D: 32 parts of maize meal to 8 parts of fish meal

subQuestions.questionText:
A new-born ruminant differs from a mature ruminant because:
(i) The forestomach is underdeveloped
(ii) Only the abomasum is functional
(iii) Milk flows through the oesophageal groove
(iv) The rumen is fully functional
Choose the CORRECT combination:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A - (i), (ii) and (iii) (2 marks)
In a new-born (milk-fed) ruminant the forestomach (rumen, reticulum, omasum) is undeveloped, only the abomasum is functional, and milk bypasses the rumen through the oesophageal groove. Statement (iv) is wrong.

subQuestions.questionText: The following is NOT normal behaviour for a large ruminant:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B - Is comfortable when separated from others in a herd (2 marks)
Large ruminants are herd animals and become stressed when isolated. Refusing to approach a river edge, showing stress signs and following a leader are all normal.

options.A: Refuses to go towards the edge of a river
options.B: Is comfortable when separated from others in a herd
options.C: Shows stress by circling, droopy ears and sunken eyes
options.D: Usually follows a leader in a herd

subQuestions.questionText: ONE of the following is NOT a basic guideline for transporting farm animals:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D - Transport different animals together in the same compartment of the truck (2 marks)
Animals of different ages, sizes, sexes and species must be separated during transport. The other options are correct guidelines.

options.A: The floor of the truck must not be slippery
options.B: Allow animals to cross a road when it is not busy
options.D: Transport different animals together in the same compartment of the truck

subQuestions.questionText: Diseases that are long lasting and occur repeatedly in the same animal:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A - Chronic (2 marks)
Chronic diseases develop slowly, last a long time and tend to recur. Acute and pre-acute diseases have a short, severe course; zoonotic diseases are those transmissible to humans.

subQuestions.questionText:
The following are preventative measures for internal parasites:
(i) Remove manure from the animal kraal
(ii) Spraying of medication
(iii) Resting infested pastures
(iv) Rotational grazing
Choose the CORRECT combination:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C - (i), (iii) and (iv) (2 marks)
Removing manure, resting infested pastures and rotational grazing break the life cycle of internal parasites. Spraying of medication (ii) is used against external parasites.

subQuestions.questionText: A part that is located between the body of the uterus and the vagina:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D - Cervix (2 marks)
The cervix is the narrow, thick-walled 'neck' of the uterus, lying between the body of the uterus and the vagina.

subQuestions.questionText: The scrotum encloses the primary reproductive organ that …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C - produces spermatozoa and testosterone (2 marks)
The testis is the primary (essential) male reproductive organ; it produces the gametes (spermatozoa) and the male sex hormone (testosterone).

options.A: produces the carrier fluid for spermatozoa.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether each of the descriptions in COLUMN B applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE of the items in COLUMN A. Write A only, B only, both A and B or none.
COLUMN A: A: Vitamin B2; B: Vitamin B1
COLUMN B: The deficiency causes the deformation and ulceration of the cornea of an eye leading to blindness
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: None (2 marks)
Deformation and ulceration of the cornea (xerophthalmia) is a symptom of vitamin A deficiency, not of vitamin B1 or vitamin B2 deficiency.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether each of the descriptions in COLUMN B applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE of the items in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: A: Grinding; B: Roasting
COLUMN B: Improves the digestibility of grain feeds
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Both A and B (2 marks)
Both grinding (mechanically reducing the particle size) and roasting (dry heating) are processing methods that improve the digestibility of grain feeds.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether each of the descriptions in COLUMN B applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE of the items in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: A: Infra-red light; B: Thermometer
COLUMN B: Equipment used to provide warmth for piglets
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: A only (2 marks)
An infra-red lamp is used to keep piglets warm in the creep area. A thermometer only measures temperature.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether each of the descriptions in COLUMN B applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE of the items in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: A: Bright eyes; B: Alert and lively
COLUMN B: A sign of poor health in farm animals
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: None (2 marks)
Bright eyes and being alert and lively are signs of good health, not poor health.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether each of the descriptions in COLUMN B applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE of the items in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: A: Allantois; B: Amnion
COLUMN B: Contains the fluid that protects the foetus from injuries
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: B only (2 marks)
The amnion is the innermost foetal membrane; it contains the amniotic fluid that cushions and protects the foetus. The allantois stores foetal wastes and helps form the placenta and umbilical cord.

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description. Write only the word/term.
A protein that contains all essential and non-essential amino acids at required levels.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Ideal / complete protein (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description. Write only the word/term.
A system where egg layers are kept in small wire cages for their entire production period.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Battery (cage) system (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description. Write only the word/term.
Defects that new-born animals inherit from their parents.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Congenital / genetic defects (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description. Write only the word/term.
The release of milk from the udder through the action of oxytocin.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Milk ejection / milk let-down (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description. Write only the word/term.
The stage of parturition when the cervix, vagina and vulva dilate, causing the foetus to move into the birth canal.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Preparatory (stage) / dilation stage (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the UNDERLINED WORD(S) in the following statement to make it TRUE. Write only the answer.
Sucrase digests cellulose and hemicellulose into acetic, butyric and propionic acids.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Cellulase (1 mark)
Cellulase (from the rumen micro-organisms) breaks down cellulose and hemicellulose into volatile fatty acids (acetic, butyric and propionic acid). Sucrase breaks down sucrose.

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the UNDERLINED WORD(S) in the following statement to make it TRUE. Write only the answer.
Salt is a source of non-protein nitrogen that becomes poisonous to animals when consumed in large quantities.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Urea (1 mark)
Urea is a non-protein nitrogen source that is toxic in large amounts. Salt is a mineral source, not a nitrogen source.

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the UNDERLINED WORD(S) in the following statement to make it TRUE. Write only the answer.
The accumulation of fluids in and around the brain, which enlarges the skull, leading to difficult birth is hydro-foetus.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Hydrocephalus (1 mark)
Hydrocephalus is the accumulation of cerebrospinal fluid in the brain, enlarging the skull and causing dystocia. Hydrops foetus (hydrallantois) is fluid accumulation in the foetal membranes.

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the UNDERLINED WORD(S) in the following statement to make it TRUE. Write only the answer.
The stage of mating in bulls that occurs after ejaculation is copulation.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Dismounting (1 mark)
Dismounting (the bull stepping off the cow) is the stage that follows ejaculation. Copulation is the mating act itself.

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the UNDERLINED WORD(S) in the following statement to make it TRUE. Write only the answer.
The Graafian follicle is a structure that develops in the ovary after ovulation.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Corpus luteum (1 mark)
After ovulation the corpus luteum forms in the ovary from the ruptured follicle. The Graafian follicle is the mature follicle present before ovulation.

subQuestions.questionText:
The flow chart in the question paper illustrates the intake, digestion and flow of feed through the alimentary canal of a farm animal: Animal ingests feed → Digestion by teeth and salivary amylase → A → Stomach → Intestines.
Name the farm animal with the digestive system illustrated above.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Pig (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason for the answer to QUESTION 2.1.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE (1 mark):
• Presence of salivary amylase in the mouth
• Both physical and chemical digestion take place in the mouth
• The flow of feed shows the route within a simple (single) stomach

subQuestions.questionText: Identify ONE part that will assist with the ingestion of feed by the animal named in QUESTION 2.1.1.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE (1 mark): Snout / lips / teeth; Tongue

subQuestions.questionText: Name part A.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Oesophagus / gullet (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate ONE function of hydrochloric acid in digestion.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE (1 mark):
• Is antiseptic and therefore destroys bacteria / prevents bacterial growth / prevents the stomach contents from rotting
• Neutralises the alkaline reaction of the saliva
• Changes the pH of the stomach to an acid medium
• Changes disaccharides (sucrose) into monosaccharides (glucose and fructose)
• Activates pepsinogen to pepsin

subQuestions.questionText:
The diagram in the question paper shows the accessory glands of the digestive system in a farm animal: A is the large lobed organ at the front; B is the elongated glandular organ lying alongside the first part of the small intestine; C is the small sac (with its duct) tucked under organ A.
Identify part B in the diagram above.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Pancreas (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Name ONE enzyme found in part B (the pancreas) that plays a role in digestion.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE (1 mark):
• Amylase
• Lipase
• A proteolytic enzyme (peptidase / trypsin / chymotrypsin / protease / erepsin)

subQuestions.questionText: State ONE function of part A (the liver).
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE (1 mark):
• Secretes bile
• Stores glycogen / converts glucose to glycogen
• Synthesises glucose needed by the animal
• Stores water and thereby regulates the fluid balance in the blood
• Produces red blood cells and destroys old red blood cells
• Stores the fat-soluble vitamins A, D, K and E
• Secretes heparin, which prevents blood clotting
• Converts toxic ammonia (from bacteria in the large intestine) into urea
• Detoxifies poisonous substances

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the importance of fat emulsification by the liquid stored in part C (bile in the gall bladder).
subQuestions.memoText: Emulsification breaks large fat globules into small droplets, which increases the surface area ✓ for the action of the enzyme lipase ✓ (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
The table below shows the organic and inorganic components of feed and their average values per kg:
Protein 8,5 g; Carbohydrates 12,3 g; Fibre 0,0 g; Sodium 110 mg; Calcium 308 mg.
Identify, in the table above, the mineral nutrient that controls the intake of stock lick by farm animals.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Sodium (Na) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State the importance of protein in the feed. Give TWO points.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Main component of muscle tissue
• Needed to build new cells / for growth
• Repairs damaged tissue
• For the production of eggs and milk
• Needed for the production of enzymes, internal secretions and hormones / antibodies
• Plays a role in reproduction and the regulation of metabolism / biochemical reactions
• Provides support for hair / skin / tendons / ligaments

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate ONE other organic component of feeds that is NOT included in the table above.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE (1 mark): Fats / oils / lipids; Vitamins

subQuestions.questionText: The feed in the table above could be recommended to prevent osteomalacia in animals. Justify this statement.
subQuestions.memoText: The feed has a high calcium content (308 mg/kg) ✓, and calcium is needed for the formation of strong, hard bones ✓ (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
The diagram in the question paper shows the digestibility of a feed in a dairy cow: 15 kg of a feed containing 12,5 kg dry matter was consumed by the cow, and the cow excreted 3,5 kg of manure with 40% moisture.
Calculate the dry matter of the feed that is absorbed by the animal.
subQuestions.memoText:
Step 1 – Dry matter in the manure: the manure is 40% moisture, so it is 60% dry matter: 60/100 × 3,5 kg = 2,1 kg ✓ (1 mark)
(Alternatively: moisture = 40/100 × 3,5 kg = 1,4 kg; dry matter = 3,5 kg − 1,4 kg = 2,1 kg)
Step 2 – Dry matter absorbed = dry matter consumed − dry matter excreted = 12,5 kg − 2,1 kg ✓ (1 mark)
Step 3 – Answer: = 10,4 kg ✓ (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State ONE animal factor that might have influenced the digestibility of the feed above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE (1 mark):
• Age / body mass of the animal
• Type of animal / type of digestive system
• Individuality
• Stage of production of the animal
• Animal breed
• Animal health

subQuestions.questionText:
A feed has total digestible nutrients (TDN) of 89% and digestible protein (DP) of 15%. The formula to calculate the nutritive ratio is:
Nutritive ratio = 1 : (% digestible non-nitrogenous substances (DNNS) ÷ % digestible protein (DP))
Use the above formula to calculate the nutritive ratio (NR) of this feed. Show ALL calculations, including the formula.
subQuestions.memoText:
Step 1 – DNNS = %TDN − %DP = 89% − 15% = 74% ✓ (1 mark)
Step 2 – NR = 1 : (%DNNS ÷ %DP) = 1 : (74% ÷ 15%) ✓ (1 mark)
Step 3 – Answer: = 1 : 4,9 (≈ 1 : 5) ✓ (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State the purpose of feeding animals with the feed containing the nutritive ratio calculated in QUESTION 2.5.1.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE (1 mark): Production; Reproduction; Growth

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason for the answer to QUESTION 2.5.2.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: It has a high protein content / a narrow nutritive ratio / an NR narrower than 1 : 6 (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
The schematic representation in the question paper shows the types of feeds and their subdivisions: 'Types of feeds' splits into Concentrates and A; Concentrates splits into B and Protein-rich; A splits into C and Succulents; C splits into D (Protein-rich) and E.
Identify A and C.
subQuestions.memoText:
A - Roughages (1 mark)
C - Dry roughages (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the importance of A (roughages) for young ruminants.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: It stimulates the development of the fore stomach (rumen) in young ruminants (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE example of EACH of the following:
(a) B
(b) D
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) B (an energy-rich concentrate) - Maize meal / oatmeal / barley meal / rye meal / sorghum meal / wheat meal (1 mark)
(b) D (a protein-rich dry roughage) - Lucerne hay / legume hay (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
A lactating dairy cow was fed 30 kg of fish meal with a gross energy (GE) value of 21 MJ/kg of dry matter. The following energy losses occurred in the dry matter consumed: 35% in the faeces; 5% in the urine; 5% in the fermentation gases; 10% in body heat.
Calculate the digestible energy value of fish meal consumed by the cow. Show ALL calculations, including the formula.
subQuestions.memoText:
Step 1 – Energy lost through faeces = 35/100 × 21 MJ/kg = 7,35 MJ/kg ✓ (1 mark)
Step 2 – Formula: Digestible energy (DE) = Gross energy (GE) − energy lost in the faeces ✓ (1 mark)
Step 3 – = 21 MJ/kg − 7,35 MJ/kg = 13,65 MJ/kg ✓ (1 mark)
Step 4 – For 30 kg: = 13,65 MJ/kg × 30 kg = 409,5 MJ ✓ (1 mark)
(OR: GE = 30 × 21 = 630 MJ; DE = 630 MJ − (630 × 35/100) = 630 MJ − 220,5 MJ = 409,5 MJ)

subQuestions.questionText: Name the energy that remains after all energy losses from gross energy.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Net energy / NE (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
The pictures in the question paper show farm animals in different farming systems. PICTURE A shows people leading a span of oxen to plough a small field by hand. PICTURE B shows a very large herd of beef cattle held in feeding pens.
Identify the farming system represented in EACH of the following:
(a) PICTURE B
(b) PICTURE A
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) PICTURE B - Commercial (1 mark)
(b) PICTURE A - Subsistence (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason for the answers to QUESTIONS 3.1.1(a) and (b).
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) PICTURE B - The large herd of beef cattle is produced to sell and make a profit ✓ (1 mark)
(b) PICTURE A - Only a few animals are used to plough the field to sustain the family ✓ (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
The pictures in the question paper depict some of the factors to be considered for increased production in farm animals. PICTURE A shows cattle feeding from a round hay bale in a feeder. PICTURE B shows a cow with its newborn calf.
Identify the factors represented in PICTURE A and PICTURE B, which would result in increased production if properly managed.
subQuestions.memoText:
PICTURE A - Nutrition / feeding (1 mark)
PICTURE B - Breeding / reproduction (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO other factors that would adversely affect the young calf in an extensive animal production system.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Harsh environmental conditions
• Poor general enterprise management
• More prone to predators

subQuestions.questionText:
The pictures in the question paper show different facilities used in animal production. PICTURE A shows a system of connected pens and narrow passages for cattle. PICTURE B shows pigs in a pen on a floor covered with straw. PICTURE C shows cattle feeding side by side at a long trough. PICTURE D shows an open-sided barn stacked with hay bales.
Identify the facility in:
(a) PICTURE A
(b) PICTURE B
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) PICTURE A - Holding pen (handling pens) (1 mark)
(b) PICTURE B - Farrowing pen / farrowing crate (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the use of bedding in PICTURE B.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE (1 mark):
• To insulate the cold cement floor / maintain heat
• To protect the piglets against the abrasive / rough cement (concrete) floor
• To absorb moisture

subQuestions.questionText: Differentiate between the facilities in PICTURE C and PICTURE D, based on their purpose.
subQuestions.memoText:
Facility in PICTURE C - Used to feed the animals (a feed trough / feeding rack) (1 mark)
Facility in PICTURE D - Used to store animal feed (a feed / hay store) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Below is a list of tools and equipment used to handle farm animals: prodder; plastic shaker; plywood board; casting harness; nose pliers; halter.
Choose the tool or equipment from the list above that is used to handle farm animals under the condition below:
Makes a loud noise to steer pigs in a particular direction.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Plastic shaker (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose the tool or equipment from the list (prodder; plastic shaker; plywood board; casting harness; nose pliers; halter) that is used to handle farm animals under the condition below:
Is placed around the head, muzzle and behind the ears of an animal to restrain or lead it.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Halter (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose the tool or equipment from the list (prodder; plastic shaker; plywood board; casting harness; nose pliers; halter) that is used to handle farm animals under the condition below:
Delivers a mild electric shock when handling large animals.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Prodder (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose the tool or equipment from the list (prodder; plastic shaker; plywood board; casting harness; nose pliers; halter) that is used to handle farm animals under the condition below:
Is tied around the head of a large animal to make it lie down.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Casting harness (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State ONE basic guideline for handling sheep.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE (1 mark):
• Approach them calmly and slowly
• Do not catch or hold sheep by their wool
• Use a herding dog to move them
• Handle them as a flock
• They can be trained to act on a vocal command
• Catch them from behind, grabbing as high as possible on the hind leg
• Sit the sheep on its rump, squat down and take a firm hold of its back legs, keeping its head up
• Pull the animal firmly against your body
• When lifting it over a fence, do not drag it – work from the same side as the animal
• Avoid the blind spot
• No sudden movements
• Do not make loud noises / avoid noise
• Use the correct handling facilities / methods
• Do not beat or throw objects at sheep

subQuestions.questionText:
The diagrams in the question paper show the life cycles of two different parasites. DIAGRAM A shows a cycle involving a human and a pig, with ribbon-like segmented worms and egg-filled segments. DIAGRAM B shows a cycle involving a cow, a tick on the cow, grass, and clusters of eggs and young stages on the ground.
Identify the parasite in DIAGRAM A.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Tapeworm (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Classify the parasite in DIAGRAM B, based on where it occurs.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: External / ecto-parasite (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Differentiate between the parasites in DIAGRAM A and DIAGRAM B, based on their life cycles.
subQuestions.memoText:
• The parasite in DIAGRAM A is a two-host parasite / needs two hosts to complete its cycle / has a 3-stage life cycle ✓ (1 mark)
• The parasite in DIAGRAM B is a one-host parasite / needs one host to complete its cycle / has a 4-stage life cycle ✓ (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO economic implications of the parasite in DIAGRAM A (an internal parasite).
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• High feeding costs (the parasite competes for nutrients)
• High treatment costs
• Poor production / degrading of carcasses
• Loss of income / profit

subQuestions.questionText:
Poisonous plants can pose a serious challenge to the health of farm animals.
State TWO measures the farmer can take to treat animals suffering from plant poisoning.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Keep affected animals away from drinking water
• Allow small quantities of water after two days
• Administer remedies that neutralise the plant poison / strong tea / activated charcoal / laxatives
• Provide large doses of purgatives to cause expulsion of the poison
• Dose with sugar / glucose
• Keep the animals calm / in the shade

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO roles of the state in animal health.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Awareness campaigns
• Legislation / registration of medication
• Research
• Training / education
• Quarantine services
• Import / export bans
• Importation / production of vaccines
• Movement control / permits
• Veterinarian services

subQuestions.questionText:
A list of diseases that can affect farm animals is given: lumpy wool; bluetongue; paralysis; brucellosis; mastitis; redwater; heartwater; foot-and-mouth disease.
Choose the disease from the list above that can be associated with the following statement:
The occurrence of round blisters that later develop into sores on the mucous membranes of the mouth, tongue and between the hooves.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose the disease from the list (lumpy wool; bluetongue; paralysis; brucellosis; mastitis; redwater; heartwater; foot-and-mouth disease) that can be associated with the following statement:
Is characterised by brown to dark urine and is transmitted by blue ticks.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Redwater (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose the disease from the list (lumpy wool; bluetongue; paralysis; brucellosis; mastitis; redwater; heartwater; foot-and-mouth disease) that can be associated with the following statement:
Causes hard scabs that affect the fleece and also occur on the ears, face and lips.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Lumpy wool (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose the disease from the list (lumpy wool; bluetongue; paralysis; brucellosis; mastitis; redwater; heartwater; foot-and-mouth disease) that can be associated with the following statement:
Signs are high fever, nervousness, grinding of the teeth, watery diarrhoea and it is transmitted by a bont tick.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Heartwater (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose the disease from the list (lumpy wool; bluetongue; paralysis; brucellosis; mastitis; redwater; heartwater; foot-and-mouth disease) that can be associated with the following statement:
Inflammation of the udder which results in thick and flaky milk with clots.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Mastitis (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO methods of administering medication to farm animals.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Injection
• Oral administration (dosing / drenching)
• Topical application
• Vaginal administration
• Dipping / foot bathing
• Intra-nasal application
• Rectal application
• Eye-drop application

subQuestions.questionText:
The diagram in the question paper represents the reproductive system of a male farm animal, with parts labelled A to F: A is a gland high up in the system; B and C are tubes; D is a small oval organ lying against the top of an oval organ enclosed in the scrotum; E is that oval organ in the scrotum; F is the outer covering of the scrotum.
Identify part D.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Epididymis (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
State ONE function of EACH of the following:
(a) Fluid in part A
(b) Part C
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Fluid in part A (seminal fluid) - any ONE (1 mark):
• Provides nutrients for the sperm cells
• Lubricates / cleanses the urethra
• Improves the motility / mobility of the sperm cells
• Acts as a pH buffer
• Increases the volume of the semen

(b) Part C (vas deferens) - any ONE (1 mark):
• Transports the sperm cells (from the epididymis to the urethra)
• Plays a role during ejaculation

subQuestions.questionText: Name the congenital defect associated with part E (the testis).
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE (1 mark): Cryptorchidism; Hypoplasia

subQuestions.questionText:
The diagram in the question paper represents a sperm cell, with parts labelled A (the long whip-like tail), B (the head, containing the nucleus) and C (the cap at the tip of the head).
Name the process through which the sperm cell is formed.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Spermatogenesis (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the letter of the part that releases an enzyme that helps the sperm cell to penetrate the female gamete.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: C (the acrosome) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Name the cell division that results in:
(a) Secondary spermatocytes
(b) Primary spermatocytes
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Secondary spermatocytes - Meiosis I (first meiotic division) (1 mark)
(b) Primary spermatocytes - Mitosis (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
The graph in the question paper provides information regarding the hormonal levels during the reproductive cycle of a cow. Progesterone (solid line) and oestrogen (dashed line) are plotted against the day of the cycle (0 to 21, then continuing 1 to 9 into the next cycle). 'Ovulation 1' is marked near the start and 'Ovulation 2' near the start of the next cycle. Oestrogen peaks sharply just before each ovulation; progesterone rises to a plateau through the middle of the cycle and then falls before the next ovulation.
Identify the time (in days) when the levels of oestrogen and progesterone are equal towards the onset of the second ovulation.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Day 2 (of the next cycle) (1 mark)
This is where the falling progesterone line and the rising oestrogen line cross, shortly before Ovulation 2.

subQuestions.questionText: Give an explanation, based on the graph above, that indicates the cow was NOT pregnant after Day 1.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE explanation (2 marks):
• The progesterone level declined ✓ and the oestrogen level increased again ✓
• The cow went on to a second oestrus cycle (a second ovulation occurred) ✓✓

subQuestions.questionText: Describe what could have happened to the corpus luteum of the cow shown in the graph above, after Day 15.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: The corpus luteum degenerated / regressed / disintegrated (luteolysis took place), so the progesterone level dropped (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the stage of the oestrus cycle between Day 5 and Day 8.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Met-oestrus (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
The table below shows the semen volume per ejaculate and the sperm cell concentration per ejaculate in different farm animals:
Bull: semen volume 8 mℓ; sperm cell concentration 1,5 billion/mℓ
Ram: semen volume 5 mℓ; sperm cell concentration 3,0 billion/mℓ
Cock: semen volume 2 mℓ; sperm cell concentration 1,0 billion/mℓ
Stallion: semen volume 7 mℓ; sperm cell concentration 1,0 billion/mℓ
Buck: semen volume 4 mℓ; sperm cell concentration 3,0 billion/mℓ
Use the data in the table above to draw a combined bar graph showing the semen volume per ejaculate and the sperm cell concentration per ejaculate in different farm animals.
subQuestions.memoText:
A combined (double) bar graph of semen volume and sperm cell concentration for each farm animal.

MARKING CRITERIA (1 mark each):
• Correct heading (naming both variables)
• X-axis: correctly calibrated with label (Farm animal)
• Y-axis: correctly calibrated with label (Semen volume per ejaculate and sperm cell concentration)
• Correct units (mℓ and billion per mℓ)
• Combined bar graph (two bars grouped per animal, with a key)
• Accuracy (at least 80% of bars correctly plotted)

Values to plot:
• Bull: volume 8; concentration 1,5
• Ram: volume 5; concentration 3,0
• Cock: volume 2; concentration 1,0
• Stallion: volume 7; concentration 1,0
• Buck: volume 4; concentration 3,0

subQuestions.questionText: State ONE requirement for the storage of collected semen.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE (1 mark):
• Proper / correct equipment should be used
• Presence of a dilutant
• Store at 5 °C if kept for a short period
• Store at −196 °C in a canister / flask containing liquid nitrogen if kept for a long period
• Store in polyvinyl straws
• The end of the straws should be sealed to prevent liquid nitrogen entering
• The straws should be properly labelled

subQuestions.questionText: Explain how a pedometer works in detecting oestrus in cattle.
subQuestions.memoText: The pedometer records a spike in the cow's movement (and body temperature) ✓, which indicates the restlessness / increased activity caused by oestrus ✓ (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain how tail chalking works in detecting oestrus in cattle.
subQuestions.memoText: Chalk (a marker) is applied to the tail head of the cow; when the cow is in oestrus and is mounted by other cows, the chalk is rubbed off ✓, so a cow with a rubbed-off mark is on heat ✓ (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Artificial insemination (AI) is a reproductive technique used by farmers.
Indicate the action the farmer would take if signs of heat (oestrus) were detected in the afternoon.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: The cow should be artificially inseminated early the next morning / about 12 hours after the signs of oestrus were first seen (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
The diagram in the question paper illustrates the formation of multiple births: two separate sperm cells each fertilise a separate egg cell (bracket A), and these develop into two separate embryos.
Explain the process of multiple birth formation shown in the diagram above.
subQuestions.memoText: Two different ova (egg cells) are released and fertilised ✓ by two different spermatozoa ✓, producing two genetically different (fraternal / dizygotic) offspring (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Name the reproductive process that occurs after A has taken place.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Pregnancy / gestation (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
A practice was applied where the nucleus of a Holstein cow, that produced 100 litres of milk per day, was extracted from the somatic cells and inserted into the enucleated ovum of a Nguni cow that produced 14 litres of milk per day. The ovum with the somatic nucleus was then inserted back into the uterus of the Nguni cow where the embryo developed until birth.
Deduce the type of reproductive technique from the paragraph above.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Reproductive cloning (somatic cell nuclear transfer) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: The calf that will be born from the Nguni cow will be a Holstein. Justify the statement.
subQuestions.memoText: The nucleus / genetic material of the offspring was taken from the Holstein cow ✓ and inserted into the (enucleated) ovum of the Nguni cow ✓, so the calf carries only Holstein genes (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: State ONE disadvantage of the reproductive technique in QUESTION 4.8.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE (1 mark):
• The conception (success) rate is low
• It is an expensive procedure
• It is a very scientific / complex procedure
• Clones are prone to diseases / have a lower immune system
• Time consuming / labour intensive
• Expert knowledge / skills / a veterinarian are required
• Clones have a short life-span
• Reduced genetic diversity
• No guarantee of success
• Dystocia problems can arise
• Genetic defects may occur
• It alters the normal reproductive process

subQuestions.questionText:
The picture in the question paper shows a stage of pregnancy in a cow, with a well-formed foetus visible inside the uterus.
Identify the stage of pregnancy in the cow represented in the picture above.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Foetal stage (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO reasons why the stage of pregnancy identified in QUESTION 4.9.1 can be terminated before the normal duration.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Metabolic or hormonal disturbances
• Nutritional deficiencies / malnutrition
• Trauma / stress / injuries
• Poisoning / toxins
• Laxatives
• Infections / diseases
• Genetic or chromosomal defects of the ova / sperm cells
• Allergies
• Twinning
• Embryo abnormalities
• Vaccination of pregnant animals
• Dropsy of the foetal membranes
